title: Rabbi Chalafta ben Shaul
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: He is mentioned in the Jerusalem Talmud: [Berakhot ch. 1 halakhah 5, folio 10a](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Berakhot.1.5.14); [Peah ch. 2 end of halakhah 4](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Peah.2.4.10); Maaserot ch. 2 end of halakhah 3; [Terumot ch. 10 halakhah 6](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Terumot.10.6.11); [Bikkurim ch. 2 halakhah 1](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Bikkurim.2.1.8) (and cited in [Midrash Tehillim 26:7](https://www.sefaria.org/Midrash_Tehillim.26.7)); [Shabbat ch. 4 halakhah 2](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Shabbat.4.2.8); [Moed Katan ch. 1 beginning of halakhah 9](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Moed_Katan.1.9.2). Hyman singles out the recurring formula “Rabbi Chalafta ben Shaul recited.” From this Hyman infers that he was among the reciters of baraitot. Hyman considers his name in the Bavli corrupted to Rabbi Tachlifa, as in [Moed Katan 10a](https://www.sefaria.org/Moed_Katan.10a.4): "But Rabbi Tachlifa bar Shaul recited: and they agree that one does not twist [ropes]"; and in Dikdukei Soferim the reading is Rabbi Chalafta ben Shaul. Hyman identifies two errors in the formula he quotes from [Zevachim 93b](https://www.sefaria.org/Zevachim.93b.3): “For it was taught: Rabbi Tachlifa bar Shaul says.” First, he argues that Chalafta was not a tanna of the Mishnaic period and that the formula should be “Rabbi … recited,” as in the parallel at [Menachot 7b](https://www.sefaria.org/Menachot.7b.7). Second, he argues for “Rabbi Chalafta ben Shaul,” the reading he attributes to Dikdukei Soferim.[^3]

For the formula “Rabbi Tachlifa bar Shmuel recited” in [Megillah 23b](https://www.sefaria.org/Megillah.23b.3), Hyman likewise prefers “Rabbi Chalafta bar Shaul,” the reading he attributes to Dikdukei Soferim. He is mentioned in [Berakhot 29a](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.29a.10), where they said: "These seven [blessings] of Shabbat correspond to what? Rabbi Chalafta ben Shaul said: Corresponding to the seven voices that David said over the waters," etc.

notes.text: Hyman first characterizes him as a reciter of baraitot, then denies that the disputed formula should place him among the tannaim of the Mishnaic period. His preferred Chalafta/Tachlifa and Shaul/Shmuel readings remain attributed textual judgments.

The inspected Moed Katan 10a reads Rav Tachlifa bar Shaul reciting the rope-twisting rule. Hyman prefers Chalafta and distinguishes the reciter formula from the disputed tannaitic formula. The exact Dikdukei Soferim readings were not inspected; neither a baraita reciter nor this occurrence automatically establishes a Mishnaic-era identity.

The text at [Zevachim 93b:3](https://www.sefaria.org/Zevachim.93b.3) reads “For it was taught: Rabbi Chalafta bar Shaul says,” already with Chalafta but still with the formula Hyman would emend. The linked Yerushalmi passages use forms of the reciter formula, with both ben and bar; [Midrash Tehillim 26:7](https://www.sefaria.org/Midrash_Tehillim.26.7) preserves a related teaching on death with different day counts from [Jerusalem Talmud Bikkurim 2:1:8](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Bikkurim.2.1.8). Hyman gives Menachot 7a and Megillah 23a. The parallel in [Menachot 7b:7](https://www.sefaria.org/Menachot.7b.7) has Rav Tachlifa ben Shaul reciting the same teaching. [Megillah 23b:3](https://www.sefaria.org/Megillah.23b.3) reads Rav Tachlifa bar Shmuel.
